questions.topic: Pub/Sub: Topics, Subscriptions, and Delivery Guarantees
questions.question: What does a Pub/Sub topic receive?
options: Acknowledgements returned by each subscriber once its processing has completed
Change events read directly from a source database's transaction log by the service
Messages that publishers send to it, which every attached subscription then copies
The offsets each consumer group has committed while reading the stream in order

questions.topic: Pub/Sub: Topics, Subscriptions, and Delivery Guarantees
questions.question: Why create separate subscriptions for analytics and alerting?
options: Each application then receives every message and tracks its own acknowledgements
A topic holds only one subscription, so a second consumer needs a second topic
Separate subscriptions let the two applications share one cursor over the topic
Separate subscriptions load-balance the same messages across both applications

questions.topic: Pub/Sub: Topics, Subscriptions, and Delivery Guarantees
questions.question: What should a standard at-least-once subscriber assume?
options: That messages arrive exactly once, so a sink can safely apply each one blindly
That messages arrive in publish order, so a later message supersedes an earlier
That acknowledging before processing is safe, since the deadline extends itself
That a message can be redelivered, so its sink has to be idempotent

questions.topic: Pub/Sub: Topics, Subscriptions, and Delivery Guarantees
questions.question: What scope supports Pub/Sub exactly-once delivery?
options: Push subscriptions delivering to any HTTPS endpoint, in every region worldwide
Pull subscriptions, within the regional scope the service documents for it
Every external database write the subscriber performs after it reads a message
Duplicate publishes an application makes of the same business event to a topic

questions.topic: Pub/Sub: Topics, Subscriptions, and Delivery Guarantees
questions.question: Why can one ordering key become a bottleneck?
options: Its messages must progress in order, so they cannot use the parallelism other keys get
Enabling an ordering key disables publishing to the topic from other publishers
Every ordering key is assigned a separate topic, so a hot key exhausts topic quota
An ordering key forces every subscription on the topic to share one acknowledgement

questions.topic: Pub/Sub: Topics, Subscriptions, and Delivery Guarantees
questions.question: Why does exactly-once delivery not make a database write and acknowledgement one transaction?
options: Because the subscriber acknowledges before the write, so the order is always wrong
Because exactly-once is only offered on push subscriptions, which cannot write rows
Because the external database sits outside the boundary Pub/Sub can commit over
Because database writes carry no message ID for Pub/Sub to match to an ack

questions.topic: Dataflow in Production: Autoscaling and Streaming Jobs
questions.question: What programming model does Dataflow execute?
options: Kafka Streams topologies, submitted as jobs to a managed broker cluster
Apache Beam pipelines, in both bounded batch and unbounded streaming modes
SQL stored procedures scheduled against the warehouse on a fixed interval
Datastream configurations describing a source, a destination, and its objects

questions.topic: Dataflow in Production: Autoscaling and Streaming Jobs
questions.question: What does Streaming Engine do?
options: Rewrites a streaming pipeline into equivalent batch jobs run on a fixed schedule
Removes per-key state limits so a hot key no longer constrains a pipeline's throughput
Replicates the source database into the pipeline so workers read from local disk
Moves streaming execution and state off worker VMs into the Dataflow backend

questions.topic: Dataflow in Production: Autoscaling and Streaming Jobs
questions.question: Why might Dataflow not scale up despite backlog?
options: The stage has too little parallelism, from a hot key or too few source partitions to split
Autoscaling reacts only to worker CPU, so a backlog with idle CPU is invisible to it
Streaming jobs are pinned to one worker unless Streaming Engine is turned off first
Backlog is measured in event time, so it never triggers a horizontal scaling decision

questions.topic: Dataflow in Production: Autoscaling and Streaming Jobs
questions.question: Which metric best reveals stale event-time results?
options: Worker CPU utilization averaged across the pool over the last several minutes
The count of failed bundles the job has retried since it was last restarted
Watermark progress and data freshness, which track how far event time has advanced
Throughput per stage in elements per second, compared against the source's rate

questions.topic: Dataflow in Production: Autoscaling and Streaming Jobs
questions.question: CPU is low, backlog is high, and one key owns most records. What is the likely remedy?
options: Raise the maximum worker count so autoscaling can add capacity for the backlog
Turn off Streaming Engine so state returns to the workers' own persistent disks
Shift the window from event time to processing time so the watermark can advance
Reshape the hot key or shard it, so the work can spread across more workers

questions.topic: Dataflow in Production: Autoscaling and Streaming Jobs
questions.question: Why should external API calls inside Dataflow use stable idempotency keys?
options: Because an API client created per element would otherwise exhaust the worker's memory
Because a retried bundle repeats the call, and the key lets the API absorb the repeat
Because Dataflow rejects any transform whose output is not deterministic per element
Because the watermark cannot advance past a bundle that has an outstanding API call

questions.topic: Datastream for Managed CDC
questions.question: What is Datastream designed to provide?
options: Managed change data capture and replication into supported destinations
A managed runner that executes arbitrary Beam transforms over change events
An in-memory cache that accelerates dashboard queries over replicated tables
A message bus whose subscriptions each receive an independent copy of events

questions.topic: Datastream for Managed CDC
questions.question: What is needed for log-based source capture?
options: A destination table that already matches the source schema column for column
An ordering key on the source table so that changes arrive in commit order downstream
Source-specific logging enabled, plus permissions, connectivity, and log retention
A Dataflow job in the same region to relay the change events to the destination

questions.topic: Datastream for Managed CDC
questions.question: What must meet at a consistent boundary during stream creation?
options: The source schema and the destination schema, once both have been validated
The initial backfill snapshot and the ongoing stream of source changes
The source log retention window and the destination's own retention policy
The Datastream private connection and the customer's VPN or Interconnect link

questions.topic: Datastream for Managed CDC
questions.question: Which workload is outside Datastream's primary role?
options: Backfilling a source table before its ongoing change stream begins to flow
Replicating committed inserts, updates, and deletes from a supported source
Landing a change stream in Cloud Storage as a durable record of every edit
Applying stateful business deduplication and windowed aggregation to changes

questions.topic: Datastream for Managed CDC
questions.question: What can happen if an outage exceeds source log retention?
options: The stream resumes from the destination's newest row and skips the missing edits
The source begins retaining logs indefinitely until the stream has caught up again
The stream may need a fresh snapshot, because the changes it needs are gone
The destination becomes the system of record until the source is repaired

questions.topic: Datastream for Managed CDC
questions.question: Why is a running stream status insufficient proof of correctness?
options: Individual tables can lag or diverge, so keys and totals still need reconciling
A running status means the backfill has finished and no changes are flowing yet
Stream status is computed hourly, so it lags the true state by up to an hour
Status reports only connectivity, never whether the source has logging enabled

questions.topic: Kafka vs Pub/Sub: An Awareness-Level Comparison
questions.question: What is a central Kafka abstraction?
options: Subscriptions that each receive an independent copy of every published message
Ordering keys that request ordered delivery without any partition provisioning
Managed stages whose parallelism the runner adjusts from backlog and throughput
Partitioned, ordered logs whose offsets each consumer group commits for itself

questions.topic: Kafka vs Pub/Sub: An Awareness-Level Comparison
questions.question: What operational responsibility does Pub/Sub primarily remove?
options: Writing consumers that stay correct when the same message is delivered twice
Running brokers and sizing partitions, since Google scales the service itself
Defining the schema contract that every publisher and consumer must agree on
Deciding which business events have to be processed in a strict relative order

questions.topic: Kafka vs Pub/Sub: An Awareness-Level Comparison
questions.question: How does Kafka normally provide ordering?
options: Globally across the whole cluster, since brokers share one commit sequence
Per consumer group, since each group replays the log in its own committed order
Within a partition, with a record's key deciding which partition it lands in
Per topic, since a topic's records are appended to a single ordered log file

questions.topic: Kafka vs Pub/Sub: An Awareness-Level Comparison
questions.question: Why is migration more than translating producer APIs?
options: Ordering, retention, replay, transactions, and compaction all have to be remapped
Both systems expose partitions and offsets, so only the client library name changes
Message payloads must be re-encoded, since Pub/Sub rejects any binary content
Consumer groups translate directly to subscriptions, so only monitoring must change

questions.topic: Kafka vs Pub/Sub: An Awareness-Level Comparison
questions.question: What is a key distinction between Kafka transactions and Pub/Sub exactly-once delivery?
options: Kafka transactions cover any external sink, while Pub/Sub covers only BigQuery
Pub/Sub's guarantee is about delivery, not a transaction over external systems
Kafka offers no delivery guarantee at all, so consumers must deduplicate by hand
Pub/Sub's guarantee spans the subscriber's database write, while Kafka's does not

questions.topic: Kafka vs Pub/Sub: An Awareness-Level Comparison
questions.question: What is the soundest selection criterion?
options: Choose the managed service, since operations always dominate total cost of ownership
Choose the system with more partitions, since parallelism decides throughput
Choose whichever product the team has already deployed somewhere else
Match guarantees, ownership, recovery, locality, and total cost to the workload
